newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Australian sorghum market rallies.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Australian sorghum market rallies.

text.p: Sorghum prices rallied in central Queensland this week on the back of a strengthening U.S. corn market and this trend influenced Australian east coast sorghum markets, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Friday.
Internationally, the market was weather-driven, based on the dry being experienced in the U.S. corn belt, the AWB said in its weekly grain market report.
This has led to some volatility in U.S. markets which may be only a short-term phenomenon, it said.
Dry weather persisting across much of Australia saw a good level of buyer interest which was unmatched by sellers.
Domestic wheat values are also responding to U.S. corn pollination and condition and the winter wheat harvest which is recording good yields but lower protein levels, the AWB said.

Speculation on protein premiums strengthening internationally continued in the week while El Nino concerns and rain shortages in South Australia, Victoria and southern New South Wales continued to drive grower prudence is selling as they wait for firmer indications of domestic yields, the AWB said.
